visual: Compact bulbous perennial forming a mound of dramatic three-part triangular leaves in rich purple to burgundy tones.
water: Keep moderately moist during active growth but never waterlogged.
soil: Free-draining compost; Avoid waterlogging; dies back when dormant
prune: No routine pruning required. Remove dead or yellowing foliage and spent flower stems as necessary.
resilience: Easy to maintain under protected conditions and capable of entering dormancy before producing fresh growth again.
uses: Houseplants, conservatories, greenhouse displays, patio containers, hanging baskets and sheltered summer displays.
toxicity: Oxalis contains oxalates and should not be eaten in quantity; keep ornamental houseplants away from pets prone to chewing foliage.
hardinessNote: RHS rates 'Mijke' H3, approximately -5 to 1°C. In the UK it is commonly grown as a houseplant or protected container plant and should be protected from hard frost.
